payload.text:
Where the harness fixes a capture time, it states the machine and measurement it came from, because settling is a property of the ENVIRONMENT as much as the content and a value measured on one box is a lucky constant elsewhere. Converge-until-two-frames-agree is the preferred shape and is to be decided on that merit alone -- NOT as a fix for the crossfade misdiagnosis that prompted it, which AC-2.13 addresses instead. Its cost is named: convergence and the transition are the same phenomenon, so a converge loop settles correctly on a crossfade but on a CRAWL only after the animation ends, which is past the dwell. The bound therefore does real work and hitting it is common rather than exceptional. NOT SATISFIED, MEASURED 2026-09-09 by snorkeltoast against their own harness: capture times are DERIVED per slide in control and compare, so the row mostly does not bite -- but where a number is fixed, NO MACHINE IS NAMED ANYWHERE. SHOT_TIMEOUT_S 45 and SHOT_SETTLE_S 0.6 carry their measurement ("the shot lands in ~2s and the process sat for the full 90s timeout") and no host. The manifest records the Chrome version and the viewport and records no host. And the 4000ms fallback of AC-2.11's two unbounded commands is a fixed capture time with NO measurement behind it at all, which is the sharper half: a constant with neither a machine nor a reading is not a lucky constant, it is an unexamined one.
NARROWED 2026-09-09 17:50Z BY vc, MEASURED AT THE CURRENT HARNESS: THE SHARPER HALF IS FIXED AND ONE CONCRETE THING REMAINS. The 4000ms fallback is GONE. `capture` read `budget_for(...) if budget_for else 4000` and now takes no default at all, refusing without a per-slide budget, with the reasoning recorded at the site: "the 4000 is the exact latent bug capture_budgets() documents -- LIMITS permits min_dwell 2500, so on a legal reel a flat 4000ms photographs the wrong slide". Every remaining occurrence of 4000 in the harness was read rather than counted: two are a test fixture's ease value, one is a selftest case name, and the other six are comments recording the defect's history. NONE IS A LIVE FIXED CAPTURE TIME. So the half of this row that had a constant with neither a machine nor a reading behind it is discharged by the constant ceasing to exist, which is the better of the two available fixes. WHAT REMAINS IS EXACTLY ONE THING AND IT IS CHEAP. SHOT_TIMEOUT_S 45 and SHOT_SETTLE_S 0.6 still carry their measurement -- "the shot lands in ~2s and the process sat for the full 90s timeout" -- and still name NO HOST; and the manifest still records the Chrome version and the viewport and no host, verified by grepping the harness for platform, uname, hostname and node() and finding only an unrelated importlib.machinery import. THE MANIFEST ALREADY RECORDS A SET THIS BELONGS TO. Chrome version and viewport are there because they change what settles; the machine changes it for the same reason and is the one member missing. DISCHARGED WHEN the manifest records the host alongside the Chrome version and the viewport, and the two constants say which box their measurement came from. Converge-until-two-frames-agree remains the preferred shape and remains undecided on its own merits; it is not required by this row and must not be smuggled in by it.
